description:
## Background

The Graph overlay can inspect the selected Issue, but Issue Detail contains several internal navigation surfaces: parent, blockers, blocked Issues, and Child Issues. In List mode those references preserve the current List view and search. In Graph mode they must preserve Graph scope, reveal a target that Focused would otherwise omit, and update the existing overlay without falling back to List.

The reusable Issue Detail interface exists specifically so callers can supply the correct destination semantics.

Triage: ready-for-agent.

## What to build

Make every Issue Reference inside Graph Issue Detail navigate to another selected Graph entry while preserving scope and revealing the target in Focused.

## Technical Approach

- Supply Graph-specific href construction and user-driven selection behavior to the reusable Issue Detail presentation.
- Parent, `blockedBy`, `blocks`, and Child Issue references target `/graph/<issue-id>` with the current Graph scope.
- Preserve ordinary anchor behavior for modified clicks while intercepting an unmodified primary activation for coordinated navigation.
- Push a new selected Graph navigation entry for each reference traversal so Back returns to the previously selected Issue.
- Treat the routed selected Issue as an additional Focused seed. This reveals a referenced closed or otherwise-out-of-scope target and adds only its direct parent and direct blockers.
- Update the overlay content and selection styling without remounting the entire Graph canvas.
- Bring the newly selected card into the uncovered canvas area without changing computed node positions.
- Retain the route and existing not-found presentation when a reference points to an ID missing from `allIssues`.

## Considerations

- Revealing a reference target does not recursively expand its upstream graph beyond the established one-step Focused rule.
- Do not switch scope automatically to Show all merely because a target was hidden.
- Copy deep link remains view-agnostic; only in-app Graph references preserve Graph.
- Modified-click behavior must remain consistent with the current reusable Issue Reference contract.
- This issue does not yet promise viewport persistence through refresh or Workspace switching; it preserves the mounted canvas during reference traversal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parent, blocker, blocked-Issue, and Child Issue references in Graph target selected Graph routes.
- [ ] Reference navigation preserves Focused or Show-all scope.
- [ ] Each unmodified reference activation pushes history, and Back restores the previous selected Issue.
- [ ] A referenced Issue outside the original Focused projection becomes a seed and is revealed with only direct context.
- [ ] Reference traversal updates the existing overlay without remounting the Graph canvas.
- [ ] The new selected card is visible outside the overlay-covered region.
- [ ] Missing reference targets keep the Graph route and show the existing not-found presentation.
- [ ] Modified clicks and copied external deep links retain their established behavior.
- [ ] `mise run doctor:react` and `mise run verify` pass.

## Test Plan

- Reusable-detail tests proving each reference kind delegates through the caller-provided destination behavior.
- Graph tests for hidden closed targets, parent references, dependency references, Child Issues, missing targets, and exact one-step expansion.
- Navigation tests for A → B → Back to A in both Focused and Show-all scopes.
- Mount-stability assertions ensure reference traversal does not recreate the canvas.
- Run the canonical `mise run verify` gate.

comments.text: Graph Issue Detail now supplies Graph hrefs and the coordinator's selection callback to the reusable presentation. Parent, blocker, blocked, and Child Issue references push selected Graph entries, preserve scope, reveal hidden selected targets through the existing focused projection, and restore prior selection through Back. Added integration coverage for a closed Child Issue traversal. mise run ts:check, ts:typecheck, and ts:test pass (408 tests).

title: Follow Issue References within Graph
